title: Semantic Segmentation: U-Net Shape and Mask Metrics

questions.question: Which pair of shapes does pixel_cross_entropy expect?
options: Logits (N,C,H,W) and integer targets (N,H,W)
Logits (N,H,W,C) and one scalar label per image
One-hot logits (N,H,W) and RGB targets (N,H,W,3)
Boxes (N,4) and class scores (N,C)
questions.explanation: The class axis stays in NCHW logits while each target pixel stores one integer class ID in NHW.

questions.question: Why does softmax in the segmentation lesson subtract a maximum per pixel?
options: To remove the background class from every mask
To keep exponentials finite while preserving each pixel's class probabilities
To make the target mask continuous for bilinear resizing
To convert NHW targets into RGB images
questions.explanation: A shared shift along the class axis leaves the probability ratios unchanged and prevents overflow for large logits.

questions.question: What does dice_loss measure in this implementation?
options: The number of pixels that differ after argmax, with no class weighting
The IoU of only the background class
One minus the mean per-class soft overlap between probabilities and one-hot targets
The number of decoder levels in the U-Net trace
questions.explanation: Dice forms 2*intersection/(probability mass + target mass) per class, averages those scores, and returns one minus that average.

questions.question: What does iou_per_class return for a class absent from both prediction and target?
options: 1.0, because absence is a perfect match
0.0, because every absent class is a false negative
The image's average RGB value
NaN, because the union is zero and the class is undefined for that batch
questions.explanation: The helper leaves the result as NaN when union is zero so callers can exclude undefined classes from a macro average.

questions.question: For unet_shape_trace((1,3,32,32), levels=2, base=8), what is the bottleneck shape?
questions.explanation: Two encoder levels halve 32 to 16 and then 8, while doubling the base channel plan to 8*2^2 = 32 at the bottleneck.

questions.question: Why does synthetic_segmentation use nearest-neighbor semantics for a categorical mask in a real pipeline?
options: Nearest interpolation guarantees the model will reach high IoU
Smooth interpolation would invent fractional class IDs between neighboring pixels
It converts every mask into a one-hot RGB photograph
It is required only for logits, not for integer targets
questions.explanation: Class IDs are categorical; resizing them with a smooth image interpolator can create values that are not valid labels.
